# sendgrid_api_key (Resource)

Manages a SendGrid API key. See the [API Key Permissions List](https://docs.sendgrid.com/api-reference/how-to-use-the-sendgrid-v3-api/authorization) for available scopes.

~> SendGrid never returns an API key's secret value after creation. Destroying and recreating this resource is the only way to obtain a new secret; there is no way to recover a lost one.

~> SendGrid automatically adds `2fa_required`, `sender_verification_eligible`, and/or `sender_verification_legacy` to some keys' scopes regardless of what is requested. This provider ignores those scopes when they are not explicitly present in `scopes` to avoid permanent diffs.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "sendgrid_api_key" "mail_send" {
  name   = "mail-send-key"
  scopes = ["mail.send"]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) A descriptive name for this API key. Does not need to be unique.

### Optional

- `scopes` (Set of String) The permissions granted to this API key. Omitting this grants Full Access; the granted scopes are then read back from the API into state.

### Read-Only

- `api_key` (String, Sensitive) The API key secret. Only ever populated at creation time.
- `id` (String) The API key ID.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sendgrid_api_key.mail_send <api_key_id>
```
